note: Every other limit in Driftwatch is a design value. All demo data is simulated.

items.title: NASA Space Flight Human-System Standard, Volume 1: Crew Health, Revision B
items.usedFor: Radiation: the career effective dose requirement (requirement V1 4030) and the design requirement for a reference solar particle event (requirement V1 4031). The reference event is shown as context and is not used in scoring.

items.title: NASA Space Flight Human-System Standard, Volume 1: Crew Health, Revision C
items.usedFor: BMD and strength tracker: the strength at or above 80% of baseline limit (requirement V1 4024) and the hip and spine BMD at or above 95% of pre-mission values limit (requirement V1 4027). The other limits, point weights and cut-offs are design values.

items.title: NASA Office of the Chief Health and Medical Officer technical brief on radiation protection, Revision E
items.usedFor: Radiation: the career effective dose requirement as summarised from NASA-STD-3001.

items.title: NASA Office of the Chief Health and Medical Officer technical brief on carbon dioxide
items.usedFor: Environment: the 3 mmHg limit for the 1-hour average cabin CO2 and the 2.5 mmHg 7-day average.

items.title: NASA Office of the Chief Health and Medical Officer technical brief on bone loss
items.usedFor: Gravity: 6 to 7 exercise sessions a week. BMD and strength tracker: the 95% of baseline hip and spine BMD limit. Nutrition: the 35 to 90 ng/mL vitamin D range.

items.title: NASA CCMC DONKI (Space Weather Database Of Notifications, Knowledge, Information): solar energetic particle events
items.usedFor: Radiation: a context line with the latest event. The events are a real NASA sample saved for May to June 2024 (or live, when a key is set). DONKI gives no flux or dose, so the events are not scored, and the scenario values stay simulated.

items.id: NASA NTRS: Behavioral Challenges of a Mars Mission
items.title: NASA Technical Reports Server paper, Behavioral Challenges of a Mars Mission
items.usedFor: Isolation: context for sleep on the ISS, stress ratings, the reaction check and scheduled contact with ground and family. The Isolation limits themselves are design values.

items.title: NOAA Space Weather Prediction Center, Space Weather Scales: Solar Radiation Storms, S1 to S5
items.usedFor: Radiation: the solar proton flux steps (S1 at 10 pfu up to S5 at 100000 pfu). How the steps map to points is a Driftwatch prototype, not a NOAA value.

items.title: NOAA GOES satellite integral proton flux at 10 MeV and above
items.usedFor: Radiation: the flux indicator uses the same quantity and unit (pfu). The scenario flux values are simulated, not downloaded.
